detail.text: I need to implement rate limiting for auth (signup/login) and link creation. Let me first explore the existing codebase to understand the structure.
The rate limiting code already exists. Let me read the existing test file to understand what's there and what needs fixing based on the findings about shared state pollution.

The issue is clear: the rate limiters are package-level globals that persist across tests, causing flaky order-dependent failures. The findings note this explicitly. I need to make the rate limiters per-App (or resettable) so tests don't pollute each other.

Let me also check how the other test files work to understand the full picture:

todos.content: Refactor rate limiters from package-level globals to per-App instances in New()
Update test to use unique RemoteAddr and verify isolation
Run bash check to verify everything passes

detail.text:
Now I understand the problem. The global `authLimiter` and `linkLimiter` persist across all tests in the `server` package. When `TestRateLimitLogin` runs, it fills up the auth limiter for key `"192.168.1.1:12345"`, and any subsequent test using that same RemoteAddr would get 429.

The fix is to make the rate limiters part of the `App` struct (or at least resettable per-test). Since the middleware functions are closures created at route registration time in `New()`, I can create fresh limiters inside `New()` and capture them in the closures. This way each `App` instance gets its own limiters, and tests creating separate `App` instances won't interfere.
Now let me refactor the rate limiters to be per-App. I'll modify `routes_ratelimit.go` to remove the global vars and instead create them inside `New()`, and update `server.go` accordingly.
Now update `server.go` to create the limiters inside `New()` and pass them to the middleware:

todos.content: Refactor rate limiters from package-level globals to per-App instances in New()
Update test to use unique RemoteAddr and verify isolation
Run bash check to verify everything passes

detail.text: Now the test already creates its own `App` via `New(Config{DataDir: t.TempDir()})`, so it gets fresh limiters. The signup request doesn't set RemoteAddr, but that's fine since each App has its own limiter now. However, I should also make sure the signup request uses the same RemoteAddr to properly account for the auth limiter (signup also counts toward the 10/min limit). Let me update the test to be more robust:

todos.content: Refactor rate limiters from package-level globals to per-App instances in New()
Update test to use unique RemoteAddr and verify isolation
Run bash check to verify everything passes

detail.text: The key change: signup counts as 1 auth attempt, so we only need 9 more logins (total 10), then the 11th request (signup + 9 logins + this one = 11) should get 429. Also using a unique RemoteAddr to avoid any collision with other tests.
